Highland Health Providers (HHP) uses revenue generated through the 340B Drug Pricing Program to expand access to care, improve patient outcomes, and reduce financial barriers for the medically underserved patients we serve. The program has allowed HHP to reinvest savings directly into services that would not otherwise be financially sustainable in our rural community.
340B revenue has also enabled HHP to expand clinical services that improve chronic disease management and preventive care. These investments include:
•	Providing registered dietitian nutrition services and diabetes education at no cost to patients, improving self-management of chronic conditions and reducing barriers to education.
•	Adding a dedicated Clinical Care Coordinator to assist patients in navigating complex healthcare needs, coordinating specialty referrals, and improving continuity of care.
•	Hiring two Prior Authorization Specialists to help patients obtain timely approval for medically necessary medications and treatments, reducing delays in care.
•	Employing a Quality Improvement Specialist focused on population health management, preventive screenings, and quality initiatives that improve patient outcomes.
HHP also invested in the implementation of the Epic electronic health record (EHR) system. This significant infrastructure investment improves care coordination across healthcare settings by allowing providers to more effectively exchange health information with hospitals, specialists, and tertiary care centers. As a result, patients experience smoother transitions of care, improved communication among providers, and enhanced continuity of treatment.
Additionally, HHP's entity-owned pharmacy operates a 340B Supplemental Discount Program that provides additional copay assistance to eligible patients. Under this program, patients facing high out-of-pocket medication costs may receive prescriptions at a standardized discounted price based on insurance remits, deductibles, and medication acquisition costs. This supplemental assistance helps ensure that cost does not become a barrier to medication adherence.
Collectively, these investments demonstrate HHP's commitment to reinvesting 340B program savings into expanded access, enhanced clinical services, improved care coordination, health information technology, and direct financial assistance for patients. The 340B program has allowed HHP to strengthen the healthcare safety net while improving the quality, affordability, and accessibility of care for the rural communities we serve.
